about: EAGLE-I dip census behind the 2026-11-08 decision-log entry (dropout rule). Written by a Claude agent (workflow wf_9cf7f578-efe, 'dropout census') from the Ian, Ida and Uri extracts in data/interim. Event 'kind' labels are the agent's judgement; utility names are inferred, not data.
truncated_note: The events list holds 100 curated events: every large Ian-window event, the big Ida and Uri ones, 8 quiet-time Florida state-total V's, and long dropouts found by residual tracking. The full machine census has 741 V-dip events (FL 303, LA 166, MS 39, TX 233; automatic draft labels give 158 artifact and 583 unclear). Most of the rest are quiet-time state-total jitter of 1,000-5,000 customers, or chains of overlapping county dips during Uri's rotation; there, merging makes 'events' up to 82 runs long, so read them as oscillation, not single dips. There are also 139 long down-then-up candidates over 12 runs (FL 47, LA 19, MS 4, TX 69). Many are quiet-time records that vanish and reappear (Osceola 1,202 to 0 to 1,204 over 105 runs; Duval 5,396 to 0 to 5,595 over 90 runs; Jackson TX 2,496 to 4 to 2,496 over 57 runs). Inside Uri, some may be real block switching. 3 more long stretches were found only by residual tracking: TECO 2022-09-29 15:15-21:45, and DEMCO-like 2021-08-30 02:15-11:30 and 2021-08-31 17:15 to 09-01 22:15. n_events_total = 741 + 139 + 3 = 883. The lists overlap a little; for example Lee 10-03 and the Sep 30 PRECO-like stretch appear in more than one. The full machine census (dip_event_census.csv and four related files) was a set of working files and is not in the repo. Only the 100 curated events are kept here.
utility_attribution: The utility names are an inference, not data. EAGLE-I county rows carry no utility field, and the names come from public knowledge of service territories, which I did not check against any source. What the data does show: which counties dip together in the same runs, and frozen residuals that come back in separate runs. FPL: 9 stretches between 09-27 and 10-08 (two small ones on 09-27 at 06:30-09:45 and 11:45-12:45; a partial one on 09-28 at 21:00; 09-29 09:15-10:45; 10-01 13:45-14:00; 10-04 07:45; 10-07 17:15; 10-07 19:00; 10-08 00:30). At 09-29 09:15, 12 counties go to 0-4 (Sarasota, Manatee, Brevard, Indian River, Okeechobee, DeSoto, Palm Beach, Martin, Miami-Dade, Glades, Broward, St. Johns). Lee, Collier, Charlotte, St. Lucie, Volusia, Flagler, Hendry, Seminole and Putnam keep residuals. That is FPL's east-coast and southwest footprint, so the Brief's Sep 29 09:15-10:45 dip is an FPL dropout, with a PRECO-like feed also missing at 09:15. TECO (Tampa Electric): Hillsborough collapses while Polk and Pasco drop partly, in 26 stretches and 60 runs from 2022-09-28 18:30 to 10-02 16:15, including 27 runs on 09-29 at 15:15-21:45. The Brief's 09-29 11:30 dip is one of them. Hillsborough 216,947 to 1,214 to 213,839, Polk -71,674 and Pasco -7,386 account for 294,793 of a 270,136 net drop, so it is an artifact. Duke Energy Florida: Pinellas reads explicit 0 in 3 stretches (9 runs, 09-29 19:45 to 23:00), with Highlands at 688 and Orange, Seminole, Volusia, Lake, Osceola, Polk and Pasco dropping partly. LCEC (Lee County Electric Cooperative; Lee, Collier, Charlotte, Hendry): 4 stretches (09-30 07:00-07:15, 09-30 13:45, 10-01 20:45-21:30, 10-03 20:15-23:30), plus maybe the Lee-only dips on 10-07, 10-16 and 10-21. In the Brief's Sep 30 07:00-07:15 dip, the counties that dipped and came back are exactly Lee (-171,345), Collier (-37,914, 24,514 back), Charlotte (-2,658) and Hendry (-250, exact). Lee's drop is close to its non-FPL residual the day before (175,437 at 09-29 09:15), so the missing feed is the non-FPL one: LCEC-like. PRECO-like (Peace River Electric Cooperative?): Hardee goes to 0, 20 or 30, Manatee -24k to -34k and DeSoto -1,028, in 5 stretches (09-29 01:00-09:15, 09-30 05:45, 07:45, 08:45-13:15, 13:45). SECO-like small dips: Lake, Marion, Sumter, Citrus (09-30 03:30, 08:30). Louisiana, DEMCO-like (Dixie EMC: Livingston, East Baton Rouge, Ascension, St. Helena, East and West Feliciana): St. Helena residual of 1,684-1,705, later 1,694 or 1,120, in 8 stretches from 08-30 02:15 to 09-06 07:15, two of them long (38 and 117 runs). The St. Tammany and Washington dip on 09-02 00:00 may be a single co-op. Entergy-like NULL runs: Jefferson, Orleans, Lafourche, Plaquemines, St. Bernard, Assumption, Iberville, St. Charles, St. James (LA 08-30 17:30, 18:30, 09-07 22:00), and Hinds, Madison, Pike, Warren in Mississippi 15 min later (08-30 17:45, 18:45). Coast Electric-like: Pearl River and Hancock (MS 08-31 00:45-01:30). Texas, CenterPoint-like: Harris at 3,000 or less with 100,000 or more on both sides in 8 stretches (16 runs, 02-16 06:00 to 02-17 21:30). Its residual is 2,908-2,915, Fort Bend is NULL or absent, and Brazoria, Galveston, Chambers and Waller drop partly. Central Texas EC-like: Gillespie, Kerr, Mason, Kendall and Llano together in 6 stretches (02-11 22:30 to 02-20 00:00).
missing_state_runs: Runs with no rows at all for the state. FL 2022 extract: 6,429 of 6,432 slots present. The only empty runs are 2022-10-18 23:15, 2022-10-19 00:15 and 2022-10-19 00:30, exactly the 3 runs missing nationally in eaglei_2022_runs (35,037 of 35,040). No run is missing for Florida alone. Ida extract: 5,854 of 5,856 slots; 2021-08-19 00:30 and 2021-08-29 23:00 have no rows for Louisiana or Mississippi, and no run is missing for only one of them. Uri extract: 4,796 of 4,800; no Texas rows at 2021-01-23 14:00, 2021-01-29 17:00, 2021-02-18 15:15 and 2021-02-23 18:30. Whether these are national gaps is unknown, because there is no 2021 run file on disk. Cases the state-missing rule cannot see: (1) 2021 NULL runs. At 2021-08-19 14:45, 50 of 62 Louisiana rows are NULL (known total 3,363 to 155 to 3,456) and 13 of 46 Mississippi rows are NULL (2,062 to 1,445 to 2,164). (2) The 2021 extracts have no explicit 0 rows at all (smallest present value 1), and they hold 2,270 NULL rows (Ida) and 8,325 (Uri). Most NULLs sit between zero or absent neighbours (LA 39%, MS 70%, TX 55% have 0 on both sides), so NULL often stands for 0. But 80 NULL cells have 1,000 or more on both sides. (3) Partial feed dropouts leave the state live while one utility's counties read 0, a frozen residual, or NULL; see the events list.
absent_county_findings: Lee (12071) has no row in 107 live Florida runs, all between 2022-08-23 11:30 and 2022-09-25 02:30, in 18 stretches of 2 to 18 runs. The Lee rows on either side read 0 to 93. None of these runs falls between 2022-09-28 and 2022-10-15 (0 runs). Lee has 10 explicit 0 rows, the latest at 2022-09-27 12:00. Counties absent while the nearest known rows on both sides are 1,000 or more: FL 23 cells (Osceola 2022-09-27 17:30 with 2,154; Duval 2022-10-17 07:15 and 08:00-12:15, 19 cells with 2,858-2,882; Hillsborough 2022-10-25 06:45-07:00 with 1,145; Duval 2022-10-25 14:30 with 4,983); LA 0; MS 0; TX 77 cells (for example Fort Bend 2021-02-16 00:45-01:00 with 31,229; Fort Bend and Chambers at 2021-02-17 21:30, together 157,137; Rains, Lee and Washington on 2021-02-17; Guadalupe, Bandera and Denton on Feb 23-26; Wilbarger 2021-03-01 22:00-23:00). NULL rows with 1,000 or more on both sides: LA 43 (13 at 2021-08-30 17:30, 19 at 18:30, 10 at 2021-09-07 22:00, Ouachita at 2021-08-19 14:45); MS 4 (Madison and Pike at 2021-08-30 17:45 and 18:45); TX 33 (Harris NULL at 06:00 on 6 days, all 6 of its NULL rows; Fort Bend NULL in 18 runs on 2021-02-16 with neighbours up to 71,616; Rains, San Jacinto, Marion, Upshur). The bigger problem is not absence. During dropouts, counties usually stay PRESENT with an explicit 0 or a frozen residual. At 2022-09-29 09:15, Sarasota, Manatee, Palm Beach, Martin, Miami-Dade, Okeechobee, Indian River, Glades and DeSoto are explicit 0, and Florida's zero rows per run go from 9 to 18. Pinellas is explicit 0 for 7 runs at 2022-09-29 19:45-21:15 and again at 21:45 and 23:00. Hillsborough is explicit 0 at 2022-09-30 12:15. Residuals: Hillsborough 1,214 or 1,210, Harris 2,908-2,915, St. Helena 1,694. Present rows at 1% or less of neighbours that are 1,000 or more on both sides: FL 40 (14 of them explicit 0), LA 1, MS 4, TX 29. So 'explicit 0 rows mean 0' is false during feed dropouts.

real_hard_cases.description: Real surge with artifacts woven through it. State 842,719 at 18:00 to 2,189,848 at 06:00. Lee 269,292 to its peak of 456,573 at 00:00, then 425,713. Collier 131,356 to 212,513. Charlotte 60,257 to 125,744 at 20:00, then frozen at 125,478 from 23:00 to 06:45 (32 runs: stale, not a dip). Largest real one-run rises: Lee +30,119 at 19:15 (343,637 to 373,756), Charlotte +12,696 at 18:15, Collier +12,411 at 18:30. But 16 of the 49 runs hold a dropout (15 TECO runs plus the FPL partial at 21:00). At 22:30, 7 of the 9 runs in Hillsborough's ±60-min window are TECO runs, so its median is 1,214. Manatee's -34,315 step at 01:00 looks like restoration but is a lost feed (FL-0929-0100). A V-rule leaves the monotone rise alone, but window medians here are often contaminated.

Real restoration steps (the new level holds for 2 h and there is no rebound of 80% or more within 24 h). Lee: -29,149 at 10-07 23:15 (94,793 to 65,644), -14,749 at 10-02 02:00 (335,970 to 321,221), -14,598 at 10-05 10:00 (195,476 to 180,878), -13,555 at 10-10 02:45 (44,030 to 30,475), -11,067 at 10-06 00:45 (164,968 to 153,901), -10,653 at 10-09 13:30 (54,683 to 44,030). Charlotte: -10,690 at 10-02 01:00 (92,405 to 81,715), -6,760 at 10-04 22:00. Collier: -6,209 at 10-02 01:00 (95,058 to 88,849), -3,780 at 10-02 04:00. Every bigger one-run drop in these three counties in this window reverses within hours, so they are dropout edges (for example Lee -182,673 at 10-01 20:45, Charlotte -98,520 at 10-01 13:45, Collier -81,847 at 10-01 13:45). A rule that compares only with the hour before would flag the real steps.

Real surge: Louisiana total 429 at 10:00 on 08-29, 518,137 at 22:00, 700,224 at 00:00 on 08-30, 905,071 at 02:00 and 1,042,719 at 16:00. Orleans climbs from 478 at 12:00 to 175,435 at 23:45 in steady steps of up to +12,608 per run. Jefferson rises +18,960 at 18:15 and +18,889 at 18:45. All of these hold. The 23:00 run on 08-29 is missing for both states. Jumps that are not real: the total reads 940,376 at 11:00 and 1,012,354 at 11:45 on 08-30 (end of the 38-run DEMCO-like dropout); swings of about ±85k at 19:45-22:45 on 08-30 (DEMCO-like dips); -92,935 at 17:15 on 08-31 and +83,349 at 22:30 on 09-01 (the 117-run dropout); and the NULL runs at 17:30 and 18:30 on 08-30 (-818,381 and -891,276 against the run before).

Real rotating outages that oscillate. Texas total 135,659 at 07:00 on Feb 15, 1,346,195 at 08:45, 2,754,115 at 18:00, 3,414,788 at 03:00 on Feb 16. The 4,257,873 peak at 19:00 on Feb 16 is inflated by Brazoria 304,535 (MCC 144,164), Fort Bend 163,337 and Galveston 150,151. Then 2,731,069 at 21:00 on Feb 17, 907,414 at 09:00 on Feb 18 and 183,463 at 12:00 on Feb 19. Between 07:30 Feb 15 and 12:00 Feb 19, 48 of 400 state run-to-run changes are 5% or more and 25 are 10% or more. County V-dips (a fall of at least max(1,000, 10%) that is back to 90% within 3 h): Harris 36 (5 of them within 2%), Denton 27, Williamson 18, Fort Bend 18, Collin 16, Bexar 14, Hidalgo 5, Dallas 3, Tarrant 3, Travis 3. Fort Bend reads 43,033 at 08:45, 10,539 at 09:00-09:15 and 43,321 at 09:30 on Feb 16, between non-dropout runs. Rotation is real, but some dips are CenterPoint dropouts. Only a frozen residual (Harris 2,908-2,915) or a NULL or absent row marks them. The 69 long down-then-up pairs in Texas may be real block switching here.

Quiet-time county noise: single-run V's where a run sits below both neighbours. Florida 2022-08-20 to 09-20, among county-runs whose smaller neighbour is 1-9: 2,202 V's out of 49,175; 1,620 (3.29%) fall below 75% of both neighbours; 661 return to exactly the same value (e.g. Columbia 2 to 1 to 2 at 2022-08-20 01:00); 739 dip to 0, 601 of them as absent rows. Below 75% at the other levels: 10-99, 668 of 32,811 (2.04%); 100-999, 235 of 13,540 (1.74%); 1,000 or more, 33 of 894 (3.69%). The same rates by level for the other extracts: Louisiana 2021-08-01 to 08-25, 1.83%, 1.13%, 1.29%, 1.28%; Mississippi, 1.69%, 0.87%, 0.67%, 0.88%; Texas 2021-01-20 to 02-09, 1.87%, 1.21%, 0.75%, 0.23%. Exact-return V's (a to b to a) by level: FL 661/360/120/5, LA 273/122/55/2, MS 154/52/23/1, TX 525/167/40/29. With no level floor, a 75% rule flags 1-3% of quiet county-runs.

State-total V's of 5% or more that come from unrelated real county changes (events FL-0823-2300, FL-0908-1930, FL-0915-1415, FL-0917-1345, FL-0917-2200, FL-0918-0115, FL-0918-0600). Example: Palm Beach is restored 6,750 to 14 while Broward later rises 119 to 10,335. Florida's quiet-time total runs from 78 to 30,598, so a 'state dips' condition is weak. The state condition alone (below 95% of both hour medians) holds in 620 runs on 2022-08-20..09-20 and in 81 runs on 2022-09-26..10-15.

Not dips, but traps for change-based or %-out rules. Frozen values: Charlotte 125,478 for 32 runs (2022-09-28 23:00 to 09-29 06:45). Hillsborough reads exactly 1,214 in 29 runs and 1,210 in 10 runs between 09-28 and 10-02, all in TECO dropouts. St. Helena reads 1,694 for 117 runs. Counts above the county's MCC: Brazoria 304,535 against 144,164 (2021-02-16 19:00); St. Helena 8,619 against 4,162 and Livingston 62,364 against 56,101 (2021-09-01 22:30).
